questions.question: Which command lists running containers?
questions.explanation: docker ps lists running containers; add -a to include stopped ones.

questions.question: Which file contains the instructions for building a Docker image?
questions.explanation: docker build reads build steps from a Dockerfile.

questions.question: Which command builds an image tagged myapp from the current directory?
questions.explanation: docker build -t names the image and . is the build context.

questions.question: What is the relationship between an image and a container?
options: An image is a running instance of a container
A container is a compressed image file
A container is a runnable instance created from an image
questions.explanation: Images are read-only templates; containers add a writable layer and a process.

questions.question: Which docker run flag maps host port 8080 to container port 80?
questions.explanation: The -p format is HOST:CONTAINER.

questions.question: Which Dockerfile instruction sets the base image?
questions.explanation: Every build stage begins with FROM naming its base image.

questions.question: With Compose v2, which command starts all services from compose.yaml in the background?
questions.explanation: up creates and starts services; -d detaches.

questions.question: Which command downloads the nginx image from a registry without running it?
questions.explanation: docker pull fetches an image; docker load imports one from a tar archive.

questions.question: How do ENTRYPOINT and CMD typically work together?
options: ENTRYPOINT sets the executable; CMD gives default arguments that docker run arguments replace
CMD runs at build time, ENTRYPOINT at run time
ENTRYPOINT is ignored when CMD is present
questions.explanation: Arguments after the image name in docker run override CMD and are appended to ENTRYPOINT.

questions.question: Why use a named volume for a database container's data directory?
options: It makes the container start faster
The data persists independently of the container's lifecycle
It shares the data with every image
questions.explanation: Volumes are managed outside the container's writable layer and survive container removal.

questions.question: What does a .dockerignore file do?
options: Excludes matching files from the build context sent to the builder
questions.explanation: Excluding files shrinks the context and keeps them out of COPY.

questions.question: In a default Compose project, how can service web connect to service db?
options: Using the host machine's IP only
Via a manually created link file
Using the hostname db on the project's default network
questions.explanation: Compose puts services on a shared network where service names resolve via DNS.

questions.question: Why copy requirements.txt and run pip install before COPY . . in a Dockerfile?
options: So cached dependency layers are reused when only source code changes
Because COPY . . must be the last instruction
To reduce the number of build stages
questions.explanation: A layer is rebuilt only if its inputs change, so dependencies stay cached across code edits.

questions.question: What does docker exec -it web sh do?
options: Creates a new container named web
Starts an interactive shell inside the running container web
Restarts container web with sh as its command
Attaches to web's main process output
questions.explanation: exec runs an extra process in an existing running container.

questions.question: What does docker compose down -v do beyond plain docker compose down?
options: Also stops containers of other projects
Also removes named volumes declared in the file and anonymous volumes
questions.explanation: down removes containers and networks; -v also removes the project's volumes.

questions.question: Which command shows container web's output and keeps following new output?
questions.explanation: docker logs -f streams the container's stdout and stderr.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage Dockerfile?
options: Build tools stay in earlier stages and the final image copies only needed artifacts
Stages run in separate containers at runtime
It lets one Dockerfile push to several registries
questions.explanation: Only the final stage ships, so compilers and build dependencies are excluded.

questions.question: What does the short form depends_on: [db] guarantee for service web?
options: web waits until db accepts connections
db is started before web, but not that it is ready
web and db share a filesystem
questions.explanation: Short-form depends_on only orders startup; readiness needs a healthcheck condition.

questions.question: Which Compose configuration makes web wait until db's healthcheck reports healthy?
questions.explanation: The long-form condition service_healthy waits for db's healthcheck to pass.

questions.question: Why prefer CMD ["python", "app.py"] over CMD python app.py?
options: Shell form cannot use environment variables
Exec form is required for multi-stage builds
The process runs as PID 1 directly and receives SIGTERM from docker stop
questions.explanation: Shell form wraps the command in /bin/sh -c, which may not forward signals to the app.

questions.question: If neither the Dockerfile nor its base image sets USER, which user do container processes run as?
options: The host user who ran docker run
questions.explanation: Containers default to root (UID 0), so a non-root USER is recommended.

questions.question: What happens to data written in a container's writable layer (no volume) after docker rm?
options: It is copied into the image
It is deleted along with the container
It moves to an anonymous volume
It stays until the next docker build
questions.explanation: The writable layer belongs to the container and is removed with it.
